All 37 tests pass. The solution in `poker.py`:

- **`_rank_value`** — maps rank strings to values (`2`–`10`, `J`=11, `Q`=12, `K`=13, `A`=14)
- **`_parse_hand`** — splits a hand string into rank values and suits (last char is the suit, so `10H` works)
- **`_straight_high`** — detects straights, treating A-2-3-4-5 as a 5-high straight (the lowest) while rejecting Q-K-A-2-3
- **`_score`** — builds a comparable tuple: category (straight flush > quads > full house > flush > straight > trips > two pair > pair > high card) followed by tie-breakers, most significant first (group ranks for made hands, descending card values for flushes/high card)
- **`best_hands`** — scores all hands, returns every hand matching the max score, preserving input order for ties

Two subtle bugs caught along the way: `dict.get(key, int(rank))` evaluates `int(rank)` eagerly (crashing on face cards), and the `(rank, count)` unpacking was reversed, which made a pair of 4s score as a quad of 3s.

`poker_test.py` was not modified, and no new files were created.
